ecommerce_adapter_boundary.principle: LOCKED 2026-07-20 (owner). We support WooCommerce PRECISELY SO the site owner can run any payment gateway, any coupon plugin, any currency plugin, any tax plugin — without us knowing or caring. From an adapter, exactly ONE fact matters: is the platform order COMPLETE or not.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.what_we_read_from_the_platform: Completion status (paid / refunded, and how much was refunded). The platform order id, for reference. That is the contract surface.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.they_are_payment_RAILS_not_platforms: LOCKED 2026-07-21 (owner): 'Woo is just a payment gateway for us like Stripe or PayPal.' WooCommerce, EDD, SureCart and FluentCart are payment RAILS, exactly like Stripe and PayPal — they report whether money moved, and we own the order semantics. They do NOT get their own status vocabulary that we translate: Stripe does not tell us to call an order 'cancelled', it tells us a refund succeeded and WE decide the order is 'refunded'. Woo gets identical treatment. Consequence: status MAPS are the wrong shape — see the refunded->cancelled map at Pro WCOrderProvider.php:487, scheduled for retirement in audit/REFUND-PLAN.md D4.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.the_rail_never_changes_the_numbers: LOCKED 2026-07-21 (owner): the gateway 'should not impact how we are calculating earning and refunds.' The rail decides only WHETHER money moved and HOW MUCH the buyer got back; it never influences arithmetic. Order total comes from our service/package price (never the rail's line total); platform_fee and vendor_earnings from CommissionService::compute_breakdown(); the vendor share of a refund from wpss_get_refund_vendor_share(); ledger rows from reverse_order_earnings(); amounts stored in base currency. A $49 service refunded in full reverses the same vendor share whether the buyer paid via Woo, Stripe, PayPal, EDD or SureCart. If swapping the rail changes any persisted number, that is the bug — not a configuration difference. This is why Pro must own no reverse_* or fee math of its own: per-rail money logic is exactly how the numbers drift apart.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.what_we_do_NOT_read: Charged amount, currency, coupon/discount, tax, gateway, fees. Reading any of those couples us to whatever plugin the owner installed and puts foreign values into our order rows, our commission split and our ledger.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.what_we_price_from: OUR OWN service/package price, always. A $49 service is a $49 order — completed is completed. Vendor earnings and the commission split are computed from our list price and never move because a buyer used a coupon, switched currency, or paid through a different gateway.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.consequence_owner_accepted: Discounts and FX differences are absorbed by the PLATFORM OWNER, not the vendor. The vendor is still paid on the list price they set. This is not a tradeoff under the current model — ONLY THE ADMIN can issue a discount (e.g. a 10% special offer); vendors have no coupon capability. The party running the promotion is therefore the party funding it, which is correct by construction. It also keeps vendor earnings predictable and the ledger in one unit.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.REVISIT_IF: Vendor-level coupons are ever introduced. At that point 'owner absorbs the discount' stops being obviously correct: a vendor's own promotion should reduce that vendor's earnings, not the owner's margin, which means the adapter would need to distinguish an admin discount from a vendor discount. Until then, do not read discounts from the platform at all. Anyone reading this and thinking 'the vendor is overpaid on discounted orders' has found the intended behaviour, not a bug.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.why_services_are_not_products: The underlying reason this model differs from normal ecommerce: we sell SERVICES, not physical stock. A service price is a vendor's rate for their own labour and delivery commitment — not a retail SKU price subject to margin, inventory or promotional dynamics. Discounting a service does not make the work smaller, so the vendor's side of the transaction is fixed at their listed rate and the discount is a platform-side marketing cost. Reasoning about this code as if it were a product store is the main way people get it wrong.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.why_this_is_the_right_seam: It is also why the adapter layer exists at all (wpss_ecommerce_adapters). Every time an adapter reaches past 'is it complete?' into the platform's money, it re-couples us to that platform's plugin ecosystem and imports a class of bugs we cannot test against. See money_authorities.currency_storage.KNOWN_GAP_woo_path_contradicts_this for a live instance.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.applies_to: WooCommerce, EDD, SureCart, FluentCart adapters equally.

money_authorities._note: READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING ANY MONEY PATH. There is exactly one authority per concept — plus one UNRESOLVED split flagged below. See also ecommerce_adapter_boundary, which governs what an adapter may read from the host platform at all.

commission.rule: Never compute a fee inline. Free (ManualOrderPage, OrderWorkflowManager) and Pro (TieredCommission flat rules, SubscriptionManager plan override, Stripe Connect split, EDD orders, subscription renewals) all route through it; the Connect split reads the PERSISTED fee and never recomputes.

wallet_balance.rule: SUM over {prefix}wpss_wallet_transactions, 'pending' rows excluded. Never SUM the table inline; pass $lock = true inside a credit/debit transaction to take FOR UPDATE. Replaced the stale vendor_profiles balance column (free) and three divergent SUM copies (Pro) in 1.2.2.
wallet_balance.callers: free: VendorsPage x3, CommissionService, OrderWorkflowManager, MilestoneService, ExtensionOrderService, TippingService; pro: InternalWalletProvider x3

payout_terminal.rule: THE terminal step of every payout rail (MONEY-FLOW.md rule 2.3). Row-locks the withdrawal (SELECT … FOR UPDATE), enforces the terminal-state guard, flips status to completed and writes the wallet-ledger debit in ONE transaction via the private insert_withdrawal_debit() core. Idempotent: marking twice debits once. process_withdrawal('completed'), the admin Withdrawals page (single + bulk) and REST PUT /wpss/v1/withdrawals/{id} all route through it — no rail may keep its own bookkeeping. record_withdrawal_debit() remains the transactional wrapper for the wpss_withdrawal_processed hook listener and the 1.2.3 backfill, both idempotent on (reference_type='withdrawal', reference_id).
payout_terminal.export_rule: CSV export (WithdrawalsPage::export_csv via admin_post_wpss_export_withdrawals) NEVER mutates status (rule 2.4) — SELECT-only, keyset-batched at 500 rows.

currency_storage.decision: LOCKED 2026-07-20 (owner). Every amount this plugin persists is a SINGLE value in the store's BASE currency. Full stop.
currency_storage.rule: wpss_orders (total, platform_fee, vendor_earnings) and wpss_wallet_transactions.amount are always base currency. We do NOT store a second shopper-currency amount, and we do NOT persist an exchange rate. There is no dual-currency order row.
currency_storage.boundary: Converting is the MULTI-CURRENCY PLUGIN's responsibility (CURCY / Aelia / WCML) — exactly as it already is for WooCommerce. Those plugins do not rewrite Woo's storage; they hook Woo's price filters and hand Woo converted values. We are a consumer on the same terms: whatever reaches our storage is already base currency, and display conversion is theirs.
currency_storage.integration_seam: The actionable consequence: WPSS price reads need filter seams equivalent to Woo's price filters, so a multi-currency plugin can hook us the same way it hooks Woo, rather than needing WPSS-specific support. Service and package prices currently come straight out of post meta (_wpss_packages price, _wpss_starting_price) with no filter, which is precisely why card 10110476797 reports a base number wearing a converted symbol. Add the seam; do not add conversion logic of our own.
currency_storage.why: The ledger and vendor payouts aggregate across many orders; that only works in one stable unit. Storing shopper-currency amounts would make wpss_get_ledger_balance() sum mixed units, and would force every payout, withdrawal and Connect split to become currency-aware. Woo core is itself single-currency (one currency column on the order, no rate anywhere in core) — multi-currency is plugin territory there too, so this keeps the boundary where Woo already draws it.
currency_storage.consequence: wpss_wallet_transactions.currency is expected to hold ONE value per install (the base currency). wpss_get_ledger_balance() sums without a currency filter, which is correct under this contract and only correct under this contract — if mixed currencies ever appear in that table, the balance is arithmetic nonsense and the bug is upstream, at whatever wrote a non-base row.
currency_storage.rejected: The card's original proposal (store base currency + the rate used, convert for display) and the store-both variant were both considered and rejected as more machinery than this plugin needs.
currency_storage.worked_example: A $49 service is a $49 order, always. Whatever the shopper actually paid on the Woo store, in whatever currency, is Woo's business — our order row, our commission split and our ledger all read $49. A vendor's earnings on a service never change because a buyer switched currency.
currency_storage.card: Basecamp 10110476797 — item 3 of that card is now answered; items 1 and 2 reduce to exposing price filter seams, and item 4 (persist the refund rate) is dropped entirely under this contract.
currency_storage.RESOLVED_woo_path: FIXED 2026-07-22 (Pro 4a48c11). WCOrderProvider used to build the order from Woo's amounts — $item->get_total() / _line_total for the price and $order->get_currency() for the currency — so the vendor's earnings depended on how the buyer paid and shopper-currency amounts flowed into a ledger that sums without a currency filter. Now reads OUR _wpss_packages price via get_package_price_by_id() and stores the base currency from the raw woocommerce_currency option. Deliberately NOT wpss_get_currency(), which Pro 1.2.2 made defer to get_woocommerce_currency() — the value CURCY/Aelia filter to the shopper's currency. Verified: a Woo line charging 31.75 EUR against our 50.00 package yields 50.00, and with woocommerce_currency filtered to EUR the stored currency stays USD.

currency_conversion.rule: Never multiply by 100 inline when talking to a gateway, and never compare gateway amounts with a hardcoded epsilon. Zero-decimal (JPY) and 3-decimal (BHD/JOD/KWD/OMR/TND) currencies both break the naive form.

withdrawable_balance.authority: EarningsService::get_summary()['available_balance'] — and it derives from the wallet ledger.
withdrawable_balance.formula: available = wpss_get_ledger_balance() - pending_withdrawal - in_clearance. The ledger is ALREADY net of completed withdrawals, so completed payouts must never be subtracted again. 'pending_withdrawal' covers still-open requests (pending + approved) that have not reached the ledger yet. 'in_clearance' is the sum of ledger CREDIT rows inside the clearance window.
withdrawable_balance.rule: Never re-derive a balance inline. Both prior inline copies are gone: EarningsController::get_summary (REST) and the withdrawal-request gate in EarningsController::create_withdrawal now both call EarningsService::get_summary().
withdrawable_balance.history: Until 1.2.3 this was a SECOND authority — it summed vendor_earnings over completed orders and never consulted the ledger, so any ledger entry with no matching order row (manual adjustment, tip credit, order reversal) moved one number and not the other. A vendor was shown one balance and gated on another. Resolved 2026-07-20 (ledger wins).
withdrawable_balance.withdrawal_debits: Completed withdrawals are debited into the ledger by EarningsService::record_withdrawal_debit(), wired to wpss_withdrawal_processed in FREE (Plugin.php). It used to live only in Pro's WalletManager, so a free-only site paid vendors out without ever debiting them and the same install grew a different balance depending on whether Pro was active. Pro's listener is now removed to avoid a double debit; idempotency matches on (reference_type='withdrawal', reference_id) so Pro's existing type='debit' rows are recognised.
withdrawable_balance.upgrade_migration: EarningsService::backfill_withdrawal_debits() runs once on upgrade to 1.2.3 (Plugin::maybe_run_install). Without it, installs that never wrote withdrawal debits would read HIGH by everything already paid out and vendors could withdraw it twice. Idempotent and safe to re-run.
withdrawable_balance.clearance_note: Clearance is now derived from ledger row created_at rather than orders.completed_at, so tips, milestone and extension credits observe the clearance window too — the orders-derived version exempted all three.
withdrawable_balance.also_dead: {prefix}wpss_vendor_profiles.available_balance / .pending_balance are mutated by a raw UPDATE at src/Frontend/AjaxHandlers.php:3405 but read by NO balance path. Write-only columns — safe to retire.
withdrawable_balance.also_note: wpss_wallet_transactions.balance_after IS still read — Pro's LedgerExporter (src/Services/LedgerExporter.php) selects it for statement CSVs. Retiring the column requires giving the exporter a running-balance computation first.

money_authorities.refunded_amount_display: wpss_get_order_refunded_amount( object $order ): float in src/functions.php is THE ONLY way a display, invoice or export surface may ask how much was refunded. wpss_orders.refunded_amount stores a SENTINEL, not a plain number: NULL means 'fully refunded', a value means 'this much was refunded'. That sentinel is load-bearing for the money layer (OrderWorkflowManager::settle_refund reads NULL as 'reverse everything', DisputeService::persist_refunded_amount writes NULL for full refunds) and MUST NOT be changed to store the total. The hazard is read-side: templates/order/order-view.php read the raw column and tested `> 0`, which silently dropped every FULL refund - the buyer saw the status 'Refunded' with no amount beside it, while a PARTIAL refund correctly showed one. Its own is_full_refund branch was dead code. The helper disambiguates 'full refund' from 'no refund' via order status and returns 0.0 when nothing was refunded. Never read the column directly from a template. Commit 2dc698b.

generated.refresh_note: 1.3.1 refresh (hand-edited; manifest_refresh: agent-enumeration-only — do NOT run write-manifest.mjs against this plugin, it undercounts REST 138->7 and clobbers the file). Deltas this cycle: (1) Payment ownership is exclusive — PaymentController registers only when wpss_uses_standalone_payments() (src/API/PaymentController.php:55), so /payments/* is absent whenever a cart adapter is active; switching rails never rewrites past orders. (2) New pay-order seam: helper wpss_get_pay_order_url() + filter wpss_pay_order_url (src/functions.php:3375/3391), the single source for 'pay THIS order' across tips, milestone phases, extensions, accepted proposals, order templates, REST checkout_url and emails. Only Pro's WCPayOrderResolver implements it; EDD/FluentCart/SureCart have no pay-order rail. (3) Minor-unit integers beside every money float. (4) Notification bodies plain text; HTML composed only for email. (5) REST: added GET /orders/{id}/timeline, GET /auth/devices, POST /reviews (alias), GET /portfolio, GET /media; REMOVED the dead accept|reject order actions from the /orders/{id}/{action} enum and with them the hooks wpss_order_accepted, wpss_order_rejected, wpss_order_delivered; deliver now routes through DeliveryService. (6) REST auth answers 401 vs 403 correctly via wpss_rest_require_login()/wpss_rest_require_admin() with one wpss_not_vendor code (bare boolean permission callbacks made anonymous callers read as rest_forbidden). (7) i18n build generates .mo/.json catalogs with a CI gate. Docs: docs-audit.py extended to scan docs/architecture, docs/qa and docs/decisions, to check 'Sell Services > X' menu paths as well as 'Settings > X' tabs, and to name the retired tab/menu labels explicitly. || 1.6.0 delta (cards 10208094640 + 10208199238): ServiceOrder::get_service() guards service_id <= 0 and post_type (get_post(0) returned the global post, so proposal/sub-orders resolved their service to the rendering page); new wpss_get_order_subject() is the single resolver for an order's subject line across the admin list, admin order detail, admin dashboard and frontend order view; new wpss_record_pending_payment_method() records the chosen rail on an unsettled order and is called by both offline entry points (AJAX checkout + REST /payments/create-intent), which previously left payment_method NULL and made the order impossible to confirm. No REST routes added or removed; PaymentController::create_offline_order can now answer 500 wpss_payment_method_not_recorded. || 1.6.0 delta (cards 10208211608 + 10208142348, one shape: a guard hid a CTA and nothing replaced it): admin order detail now surfaces the order's dispute via DisputeService::get_by_order() (loud while unresolved, quiet once closed, with an explicit warning when a Completed order still carries a live dispute); the order page's review block now renders the submitted review instead of nothing, gates the CTA and the modal on the single ReviewService::can_review() authority so the review window is respected, and explains itself when the CTA is withheld. New shared partial templates/partials/review-body.php renders a Review model and is used by both the order page and the public reviews list, which previously had its own inline copy reading raw columns. || 1.6.0 delta (card 10208211769): new wpss_get_settings_url() + wpss_get_settings_sections() (filter wpss_settings_sections); all 13 `&tab=` settings deep links in Free and Pro converted to hash routing, and FIVE of them additionally pointed at the wrong section - verified against each feature's real settings render hook, not the old link (Stripe Connect and Razorpay named 'gateways' which never existed -> payments; PayPal Payouts payments -> payouts; Tiered Commission payments -> commission; Recurring Services vendor -> orders). admin-settings-nav.js gained legacy ?tab= support and hashchange handling; .min rebuilt.

portfolio_standards.account_billing_layer: ~/.claude/workflows/wbcom-account-billing-standard.md — LOCKED 2026-07-22. Applies to EVERY Wbcom plugin that takes money, not just this one. Billing identity lives on the USER via WooCommerce's billing_* meta keys (plus billing_gst, which Woo lacks), so one address is shared across Learnomy, Eventonomy, WP Sell Services, Career Board, Listora and BuddyNext with no cross-plugin dependency. Orders snapshot the address at payment so invoices cannot be rewritten by a later profile edit. Gateways CONSUME the values, never render or own them. Country and currency lists must be COMPLETE and come from one helper each — a partial list silently excludes customers rather than failing visibly. This plugin is the reference implementation.
portfolio_standards.reference_implementation: wpss_get_billing_fields() / wpss_get_billing_address() / wpss_save_billing_address() / wpss_is_billing_address_complete() / wpss_get_countries() / wpss_get_currency_registry() in src/functions.php; wpss_orders.billing_address JSON snapshot; templates/partials/billing-fields.php. Commits a86b867, 7655e99, d97f1f0, b6d18c4.
portfolio_standards.billing_display_authority: templates/partials/billing-summary.php is THE ONLY read-only billing renderer — buyer order view (templates/order/order-view.php), admin order screen (Admin::render_order_detail) and any future invoice/export all include this one partial, so the customer and the admin can never be shown different invoice detail. It accepts BOTH shapes billing_address arrives in (ServiceOrder decodes to array; admin passes a raw $wpdb row where it is still a JSON string) rather than forcing callers to hydrate a model. It reads the ORDER SNAPSHOT only and never falls back to the live profile — a fallback would show an address the buyer was not billed under. Pre-1.5.0 orders have no snapshot and render nothing. Editable counterpart is billing-fields.php; the two must stay in step. Styled in design-system.css AND admin.css because design-system.css is not enqueued in wp-admin. Commit 894161d.

hooks._note: Unique do_action()/apply_filters() literals in src/. Counts enumerated by hand for 1.3.1 and NOT re-counted since; treat as indicative, not exact. key_extension_hooks below is maintained per-change and is authoritative for documented seams.

notifications._note: In-app notifications live in {prefix}wpss_notifications. NotificationService::create() is the ONE writer (it also persists action_url, the deep link) and NotificationService::send() maps a type to its title/body copy -- add a `case` there for any new type or it silently renders the generic 'You have a new notification.' fallback. Domain event -> notification wiring lives in Plugin::define_notification_hooks(). A type that emails via EmailService MUST also be listed in NotificationService::is_email_service_handling()'s $covered_types, or the recipient gets the branded mail plus a plain duplicate.
notifications.deep_link_column: action_url (written by create() from $data['action_url'], rendered as the row title link)
notifications.known_drift: Notification::get_icon() is keyed on TYPE_* constants ('order_new', 'message_new') that are largely never written; the live icon map is in the render partial. Unifying them is an open item.

disputes._note: A dispute conversation is ONE store: {prefix}wpss_dispute_messages. It used to be two -- the opening statement and admin replies in that table, member evidence in the disputes row's `evidence` JSON -- and each surface read only one, so members saw 'No messages yet' on a thread the admin could read in full, and admins never saw member evidence. DisputeService::add_evidence() writes the table; get_evidence() reads it and is the single reader (DisputeWorkflowManager::get_timeline() consumes it rather than querying again, or every message would appear twice). The `evidence` column now holds ONLY status_note entries written by update_status() -- dispute status history, not conversation. Legacy rows are moved by DisputeService::migrate_evidence_to_messages(), gated on the wpss_dispute_evidence_migrated option.
disputes.order_surface: src/Admin/Admin.php::render_order_detail -- dispute banner on the order itself (notice-error while open/pending_review/escalated, notice-info once resolved/closed), via DisputeService::get_by_order(). A dispute does NOT force the order's status, so a Completed order can carry an open dispute; this screen previously showed status, messages, deliveries and refund controls with no mention of it (Basecamp 10208211608).
disputes.reason_column_is_free_text: wpss_disputes.reason holds free text on real installs ('Quality issue', 'rft'), not only the Dispute::REASON_* keys. Any label lookup MUST fall through to the raw value -- confirmed against sandbox rows, which contradicted the enum the code implies.

orders._note: An order does not always point at a service post. Buyer-request orders are sold off a proposal and every sub-order (tip, extension, milestone) hangs off a parent, so all of them carry service_id = 0 BY DESIGN. get_post( 0 ) returns the GLOBAL $post rather than null, so ServiceOrder::get_service() used to resolve those orders' "service" to whatever page was rendering -- on the checkout page a proposal order reported the checkout page as its service (title "Service Checkout", form posting the page ID as service_id), and in wp-admin, where there is no global post, the same orders read "Deleted". Every `if ( ! $service )` fallback in the plugin was therefore unreachable. get_service() now guards service_id <= 0 and checks post_type, and one resolver -- wpss_get_order_subject() -- answers "what is this order for" for all four surfaces that used to answer it differently.
orders.service_resolver: WPSellServices\Models\ServiceOrder::get_service (returns null for service_id <= 0; requires post_type wpss_service)
subject_resolution_order: platform 'request' -> the wpss_request post, else meta.proposal_snapshot.request_title, else 'Buyer request'
service_id <= 0 on a catalog order -> 'No service linked' (data integrity, not a deletion)
subject_surfaces: src/Admin/Admin.php (admin order detail + admin dashboard Recent Orders)
orders.subject_known_drift: templates/dashboard/sections/orders.php and sales.php still build their own card title. They are correct (they guard service_id before get_post and fall back to the request post) and add milestone phase titles the resolver does not own, so they were left alone -- but they remain a second implementation of the same label.
orders.pending_payment_method_note: Gateways normally write payment_method as a side effect of mark_as_paid(). Offline does not settle in-request, so both of its pay-an-existing-order entry points (OfflineGateway::ajax_create_order and PaymentController::create_offline_order) go through this one guarded, idempotent writer. Leaving it NULL was a dead end, not a cosmetic gap: OfflineGateway::render_admin_order_actions(), PaymentReceiptService::can_submit() and the payment instructions all key off payment_method === 'offline', so the order could never be confirmed by anyone.
orders.payment_settlement_authority: StandaloneOrderProvider::mark_as_paid -- the only writer of payment_status/paid_at; wpss_record_pending_payment_method never touches them
orders.earnings_credit_timing: CommissionService::record() on transition to completed, not at payment (escrow model)

reviews._note: The order page's review block was `if ( ! $review_exists )` with no else, so the moment a buyer submitted a review the order went silent about it - the buyer's own review was invisible to the buyer on the only page they would look for it. The same seven lines also ran a raw $wpdb query for a question ReviewService already owns, and gated the CTA WITHOUT the review window, so after the window closed the button still invited a review the server would then refuse. can_review() is now the single authority on both the CTA and the modal, and its `reason` string is rendered when the CTA is withheld.
reviews.gate_authority: WPSellServices\Services\ReviewService::can_review( int $order_id, int $reviewer_id ): array{can_review: bool, reason: string} -- enforces completed + ownership + no-existing-review + within window
reviews.shared_partial: templates/partials/review-body.php -- author/stars/date header + content + seller response, takes a Review MODEL
shared_partial_consumers: templates/order/order-view.php (buyer sees 'Your Review', vendor sees 'Buyer Review')
templates/partials/service-reviews.php (public list; wraps raw rows with Review::from_db and keeps its own Helpful control)
reviews.model_shape_note: The reviews table columns and the model properties differ by name: review -> content, vendor_reply -> response, vendor_reply_at -> response_at, reviewee_id -> reviewed_id. There is NO title column. The public list used to read raw columns and used customer_id for the avatar while gating Helpful on reviewer_id - two names for one author on one screen. Everything now goes through Review::from_db().
